source_of_truth: Metheues Clothings — T-Shirt-First MVP v2.0 (§6 brand, §13 accessibility, §17 screens)
decision_log: Stitch project scrapped as a design source on the user's instruction — inconsistency across independently generated boards.
Copy written fresh from the MVP language rather than carried over from Stitch.
Desktop width 1440 per §13; Stitch boards were 1280.

Reuse matrix: Simple Design System 'Button' exists but REBUILD — remote community library, binds to its own tokens, generic-neutral visual language incompatible with the editorial Bodoni/Manrope direction. Material 3 and Apple kits rejected for the same reason.
Figma plan is Starter: hard cap of 3 pages, so components and screens are organised in sections rather than a page per component.

Header.note: Wordmark centred structurally — outer columns FILL equally, wordmark hugs. Measured offset 0 at all three breakpoints.

Form Field.note: Input height 50px, clears the 44px minimum. Error carries the word Error as well as the colour.

Product Card.note: 4:5 image well. Sold out label sits outside the dimmed image so it stays legible at full opacity.

Footer.note: All three breakpoints. Tablet keeps four columns at 768; mobile wraps to 2x2. Muted text uses text/muted-inverse throughout.

accessibility_findings: Icon glyphs built from rotated LINE nodes do not land where the maths says — Figma rotates about the node origin, so the X and chevron came out as single diagonal strokes. Rebuilt as VECTOR nodes with explicit path data ('M 0 0 L 14 14 M 14 0 L 0 14'), which is exact and scales. Use vectors for every glyph from here.

Stone #68635D on Metheues Black measures 3.2:1 — fails AA for body text. Added Text/Supporting Stone on Dark #8A8178 (4.97:1) and Semantic/text/muted-inverse; all 14 footer supporting-text nodes rebound to it. Any future dark-ground surface must use the inverse token.

Recurring build hazard: figma.createAutoLayout() applies a default white fill. Clear fills on every container frame or cream text lands on white bands — hit twice, on the Foundations page and the Footer.
Figma query() attribute selectors cannot contain spaces — FRAME[name=Account navigation] silently matches nothing. Use children.find(c => c.name === '...') for multi-word names.

resolved.figma_plan: Upgraded to Pro with a Full seat — 200 MCP calls/day, 15/min. The Starter 20-per-month cap no longer applies.

build_hazards: Cloning a finished screen and swapping only the content column is far cheaper and more consistent than rebuilding a shell — but remember the mobile Sign out button lives INSIDE the content column, so it must be re-added when the column is replaced.
Ghost Button instances land FILL width with centred content; set primaryAxisAlignItems='MIN' (and paddingLeft 0, or 14 to match nav items) to left-align them with surrounding copy.
maxWidth on a FILL auto-layout child is the clean way to cap a wide desktop content column without switching it to FIXED.

A component variant sized with resize(w,h) becomes FIXED on both axes; any text inside that wraps then overflows and overlaps the next sibling. Use minHeight for a touch-target floor and leave the counter axis AUTO.

A TEXT node left at WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT inside a FILL column does not wrap — it overflows and is clipped by the frame. Set layoutSizingHorizontal='FILL' on every text that shares a row with something else.
On mobile, a head row holding a title column and a status pill needs layoutWrap='WRAP' or the pill squeezes the title to nothing.
An empty auto-layout FRAME defaults to 100x100 — using one as a flexible spacer silently inflates its row. resize(1,1) first, then set layoutSizingHorizontal='FILL' and layoutSizingVertical='FIXED'.

03A Product Listing Desktop nests Discovery bar and Product grid inside 'Listing body' > 'Results'; mobile and tablet keep them at the top level. Any clone-and-edit across breakpoints must branch on that.

A HORIZONTAL shell frame hugs on HEIGHT, not width: set primaryAxisSizingMode='FIXED' (width) and counterAxisSizingMode='AUTO' (height). Getting it backwards leaves the frame 100px tall with everything clipped.
layoutSizingHorizontal must be set AFTER appendChild — setting it on a node that is not yet in an auto-layout parent silently does nothing.
A FILL child inside a WRAP container shares the row rather than filling the width. To stack full-width cards on mobile, switch the container to VERTICAL rather than relying on FILL.
counterAxisAlignItems has no 'STRETCH' — use layoutSizingVertical='FILL' on the child instead.
Check argument counts on long helper signatures: makeAdminShell(...) was called with 7 of 8 args, which silently pushed the subtitle into the title slot and dropped the page title on three screens.
Desktop admin frames need minHeight (900 used) or a short page lets the black rail hug the content and clip the sign-out block.

resize() re-fixes BOTH sizing modes on an auto-layout frame. Set primaryAxisSizingMode/counterAxisSizingMode AFTER the resize, or a shell meant to hug its content stays stuck at the resize height (A04 desktop sat at its 900 minHeight with 2600px of content clipped).

layoutSizingHorizontal='HUG' does not reliably shrink an instance whose main component has a FILL-width text child — the instance keeps a wide intrinsic width. For chip-like rows of a form component, set FIXED and resize instead.

A01 Admin Sign In.note: Centred card on a Metheues Black ground so staff never confuse it with the customer sign-in. Carries the session-expiry and audit-log notice.

A02 Dashboard.note: All seven §9.1 figures: orders today, paid revenue, awaiting fulfilment, low-stock, sold-out, recent orders, returns awaiting review. Recent orders is a table on tablet/desktop and cards on mobile; metrics stack on mobile.

A03 T-shirts table.note: 9 products covering every publish state: Published, Sold out, Draft, Scheduled, Archived.

A07 Inventory table.note: Sorted lowest stock first, with threshold shown beside the count so Low is explainable rather than asserted. Footer carries the §9.3 rules — stock never negative, manual changes need a reason and are audited.

A11 Orders table.note: Payment and fulfilment as separate badge columns per §9.4, with the search and filter set the spec lists (order number/customer/email, payment, fulfilment, date range, country, sort).

admin_table_pattern.note: buildTable(cols, rows, avail, bp) with weighted columns — each column carries a w weight, converted to a FIXED px width from the available content width (desktop 1100, tablet 684) so columns align down the page instead of splitting evenly. buildCards(cols, rows) is the mobile fallback: first column becomes the heading, the rest collapse to a middot-separated meta line, badges move to their own row. Cells are either a string or {badge, tone}.
admin_table_pattern.toolbar: searchBox(placeholder) + filterSelect(label) chips in a wrapping toolbar; footer pairs a plain-language count with Previous/Next (Previous is Disabled on page one).

admin_breakpoint_decision.rule: Admin screens are built at 1440 and 768 only. 390 is added ONLY for the handful that are genuinely phone jobs: Dashboard, Orders table, Order detail, Returns queue (plus Admin Sign In, T-shirts and Inventory, already built and kept).
admin_breakpoint_decision.reason: Dense tables and multi-section editors fight a 390px screen; the T-shirt editor alone has eleven sections. Phone versions of all 23 would cost real time and produce screens nobody maintains.

A04 Edit T-shirt.note: All eleven §9.2 sections. Main column carries 01 Basic information, 02 Description and story, 03 Images, 05 Fit and garment spec, 06 Colours and sizes, 07 SKUs/prices/inventory, 08 Care, 09 Delivery data; the 340px side rail carries 11 Publishing, 04 Collection and style, 10 SEO preview, plus a 'Worth a look' pre-publish checklist and an archiving explanation. Section numbers appear on BOTH columns so the split across two columns stays traceable against the spec. Desktop 1440x3515; tablet stacks to one column.
A04 Edit T-shirt.notable: Fit and garment spec is labelled as the source the size guide reads from, so the two never drift. Archiving copy states existing orders keep their own snapshot.

A05 Product image manager.note: Ordered grid with the first tile ringed as primary, a selected-image rail carrying alt text, colour assignment and file metadata, and a guidance card that names the one image blocking publish. Alt-text helper says what it is FOR (describe it for someone who cannot see it) rather than just demanding a value.

A06 Generate variants.note: Dialog over a black scrim. Colour x size matrix marks each cell new or exists, so the destructive question ('will this overwrite my stock?') is answered before the button is pressed. SKU pattern with a worked example; new variants default to inactive with zero stock.

A08 Adjust stock.note: Add / Remove / Set-to as Selectable Options, required reason, optional note, and a live result line ('Stock goes from 2 to 14'). States the §9.3 rule that a removal larger than stock is REJECTED rather than clamped to zero, and shows the exact audit-log line that will be written.

admin_dialog_pattern.note: dialogFrame(name, w, x, y, cardW) — a full-width frame filled Metheues Black standing in for the dimmed admin page, with a centred Soft Cream card. dialogHead(box, title, sub) adds the title, one explanatory line and a rule. Every destructive or auditable dialog ends with the literal audit-log line it will write.

catalogue_consistency_pass.problem: The storefront order and return screens named products (Origin Tee, Meridian Tee, Atelier Tee) that did not exist in the admin catalogue built later (Origin Story Tee, Nightshift Oversized Tee, Frequency One Tee). Same orders, different products.
catalogue_consistency_pass.fix: Ran one find-and-replace across pages 01 and 02: 173 text nodes on 45 screens. Names mapped to catalogue names; prices mapped to catalogue prices (Frequency One £68, Nightshift £74, Origin Story £68, Essential £58).
catalogue_consistency_pass.knock_on: The sweep also rewrote totals in the bag/checkout/confirmation flow, breaking their arithmetic (lines summed £268, total read £284). Reverted £284->£268 and £47.33->£44.67 on screens 05-09 only. The checkout basket is a DIFFERENT basket from order MC-10482 and does not need to match it.

catalogue_consistency_pass.lesson: A global find-and-replace across a design file will hit arithmetic it does not understand. After any sweep, re-read every total and check it against its own line items.

A12 Order details.note: Every §9.4 requirement: customer and delivery, immutable item snapshot (stated as such on the screen), Stripe payment intent, fulfilment timeline, internal notes marked never-shown-to-customer, tracking, cancel/refund controls, audit history. Cancel/refund copy states the stock consequence — full cancel returns stock, partial refund does NOT.

A13 Fulfilment.note: §9.5 pick-pack flow. Pick list keys on exact colour/size with SKU and shelf location; Mark packed is Disabled until every line is ticked, with the reason stated. Explains that packing sends nothing — the dispatch email fires only when tracking is added, so a packed box sitting overnight never emails a day early.

A14 Add tracking.note: Carrier, number and an auto-filled link, plus a preview of the exact email the customer receives. States that this IS the dispatch email — no separate send button — so the model matches A13.

A15 Cancel order.note: Four consequences spelled out with tone dots: money out (red), stock back (green), customer emailed, status locked. Required reason, plus type-the-order-number confirmation with the primary button Disabled until it matches. Ends with the literal audit line.

A16 Refund.note: Full vs partial as Selectable Options. Restock is a SEPARATE unticked checkbox — refunding money and putting goods back on the shelf are different events, often days apart, and conflating them is how stock counts drift. Type-the-amount confirmation; Disabled until it matches.

open_question_danger_button.question: The Button component has Primary / Secondary / Ghost only — no destructive style. Cancel and Refund currently rely on copy, consequence lists and a typed confirmation rather than a red button.

A17 Returns queue.note: Sorted so anything waiting on you sits at the top, not newest-first. Five rows covering every state: waiting, in transit, received, refunded, rejected. Footer states the 5-day escalation rule.

A19 Customers.note: Verified / Unverified / Guest as an Account column. Footer explains that guests are matched by email so their orders still group, but they cannot sign in until they register with the same address. Lifetime spend reconciles with the order data (Jordan £284 + £210 + £68 = £562).

A18 Return details.note: §9.6 in full. Condition and the restock decision are PER ITEM, not per return — one T-shirt can go back on the shelf while the other does not. Approving is explicitly separated from refunding: approval records condition and applies restock, the refund is its own deliberate step and its button stays Disabled until the parcel is received and checked.

A20 Customer details.note: Orders, returns, saved addresses, profile, consent and data requests. Contact preferences are READ-ONLY by design — changing consent from the admin side creates a record you cannot evidence. Data card states the one-month UK GDPR deadline and that erasure removes the profile, not the six-year sales history.

A09 Collections.note: Drag-ordered list, four states (Live / Live / Scheduled / Hidden). Footer explains the three behaviours people get wrong: a T-shirt can sit in several collections, removing it does not unpublish it, and hiding a collection keeps its page reachable so shared links still work.

A10 Collection editor.note: Basics, hero with required alt text, drag-ordered product list, publishing and SEO in the side rail.

A21 Homepage content.note: All seven §9.7 slots, numbered. States on the screen that section order, featured count and layout are fixed — the spec calls this a limited content system, not a page builder, and the UI says so rather than implying otherwise. Flags that the announcement threshold does NOT drive checkout.

A22 Store settings.note: The numbers checkout actually uses: delivery options and the £150 threshold, return window and collection fee, VAT, Stripe, sender addresses, staff roles, maintenance mode. Several fields name the screen they must stay in step with (announcement bar, returns page), since nothing validates that automatically.

A23 Audit log.note: Eight entries covering every auditable event §9.6 requires: refund, stock adjustment, return, content publish, dispatch, archive, price change, sign-in. Stated as append-only — nobody, including the owner, can edit or remove an entry — and kept six years alongside order records.

system_states.page: 02 · Admin & System States (below the admin screens, y=72000 onwards)

S1 Loading.note: Listing skeleton shaped like the real content so nothing jumps on arrival. Caption records the rule: fade, never pulse, and hand over to S2 after ~10s.

S2 Offline and retry.note: Names which side failed rather than 'something went wrong'. Backoff is visible (2/4/8/16s, then stop) and the bag is stated as safe on the device.

S3 Unauthorized.note: Sign-in returns the person to the page they asked for, not the account home. Offers the guest-order lookup, because most people who hit this never made an account.

S4 Order processing delayed.note: The webhook-delay state. Leads with 'payment taken, order coming', gives the Stripe payment reference that works before an order number exists, and says refreshing will not charge twice.

S5 Validation failure.note: Page-level error summary above the form, in the SAME ORDER as the fields, each line linking to its field. Messages say what to do ('Enter a postcode'), not what is wrong. Uses the Form Field error variant; nothing the customer typed is cleared.

S6 Not found.note: Explains that a missing product page usually means the drop sold through — more useful here than an apology. Caption records that 500 reuses the layout with a reference code.

E5 and E7 have no CTA. There is nothing for the customer to do and a button would only lead to a page repeating the email.
E7 sends when the refund has actually left (A16), not on approval (A18) — approval and refund are separate events in the admin.

E3 mirrors 09 Order Confirmation exactly — same order number, items and total. If screen and email disagree the customer trusts neither.

guarantees_made_structural.stock never negative: CHECK (stock_quantity >= 0); an oversell raises rather than clamping
guarantees_made_structural.stock decreases exactly once: unique index on inventory_adjustments (order_id, variant_id, kind); the decrement inserts first, so a replayed webhook inserts nothing and updates nothing
guarantees_made_structural.one checkout, one order: webhook_events.stripe_event_id is the PK; record the event before doing the work
guarantees_made_structural.server-authoritative price: price_cart(jsonb) takes only variant ids and quantities, returns real prices from the DB
guarantees_made_structural.audit is append-only: triggers block UPDATE and DELETE on audit_logs

other_decisions: order_items are snapshot columns, not joins — this is what makes archiving safe
orders and order_items carry CHECKs that the totals add up
inactive variants stay readable so sold-out sizes render disabled (§8.4)
database.known_gap: Guest order lookup cannot work through RLS — needs a server route taking order number AND email with the service role. A policy matching on email alone would expose every guest order.
still_app_level: Stripe signature verification against the raw body

security_finding.what: 001-003 left decrement_stock_for_order, restock_for_order and price_cart callable by anon over /rest/v1/rpc. They are SECURITY DEFINER, so anyone could have moved stock.
security_finding.cause: Postgres grants EXECUTE to PUBLIC by default and Supabase exposes public functions as RPC. I did not revoke.
security_finding.found_by: Supabase security advisor, run straight after applying
security_finding.fixed_by: 004_lock_down_functions — revoke from public/anon/authenticated, grant to service_role only
security_finding.rule: Every SECURITY DEFINER function needs an explicit REVOKE unless the whole internet should call it.

verified.stock decreases exactly once: PASS — first call updated 1 row, stock 3->1; replay returned 0 rows, stock still 1, one adjustment row
verified.stock cannot go negative: PASS — selling 5 against stock 1 raised 'Oversell on order ...: stock would go negative' rather than clamping
verified.server-authoritative price: PASS — price_cart ignored a unit_price_pence of 1 in the payload and returned 6800 from the database
verified.test data: removed; all tables back to zero rows
verified.note: First smoke test returned a false negative — the function was called in the same statement as the CTE inserts, so it could not see rows a sibling CTE had written. Re-tested as separate statements.

remaining_advisories: is_staff/is_owner callable over RPC — intentional, needed by RLS policies, reports only on the caller
citext installed in public schema — namespace hygiene, left alone because columns already depend on the type
webhook_events has RLS with no policy — intentional deny-all

app.migration_005: order_number and return_number now default from Postgres sequences (MC-10001+, RET-4400+). App-side generation can race; a sequence cannot. Gaps from rolled-back checkouts are intentional — reusing a number would attach a new order to an old paper trail.
app.checkout_route: Zod .strict() schema accepting ONLY variant_id + quantity, so a request carrying a price is rejected rather than ignored. Prices from price_cart(), delivery from store_settings. Rejects if the priced line count differs from what was asked for — the basket changed under the customer.
app.webhook_route: Raw body via req.text() for signature verification; claim-before-work via webhook_events PK; handles checkout.session.completed, charge.refunded, checkout.session.expired.

bug_found_and_fixed.what: A handler that threw after claiming the event left the claim row in place. Stripe retries, the duplicate guard returns 200, the work never happens and nothing reports it — a paid order sitting unfulfilled with no stock movement and no error.
bug_found_and_fixed.fix: The catch block deletes the claim row before returning 500, so the retry can redo the work. Safe because the order update is idempotent and decrement_stock_for_order has its own unique-index guard.

deliberate: An oversell does NOT fail the webhook — the payment is real and the order must exist, so it is saved and written to audit_logs for a human.
charge.refunded does NOT restock — refund and goods returning are separate events, matching A16.
lib/supabase/server.ts starts with import 'server-only' so a service key leaking into a client component fails the build.
